data.note:
Note: Reviewed unblinding — lactacystin PubChem CID 6610292 (e21) with no ChEMBL curated mechanism, but literature confirms lactacystin as canonical 20S proteasome inhibitor (PMID 39988264 describes 20S proteasome inhibitor lactacystin; PMID 27802243 reviews The Proteasome Inhibition Model of Parkinson's Disease using lactacystin). My blinded conclusion DNA replication (p 0.41) was incorrect vs annotated Protein degradation.

Reflection: Phenotype was biphasic DNA intensity (0.3 µM z+5.3 to 10 µM z-8.4, rho -1.0 e9) with monotonic cell enlargement (cell_area z+6.8, cell_nuc_area_ratio z+9.2 e2, rho +1.0 e11/e13) and modest cytostasis (cell_count z-3.5). I followed weak NSC vote DNA replication 2/4 (e6) despite very low cosine similarities 0.16-0.33, and k-neighbours split Aurora 5/10 vs DNA replication 4/10 with equally low 0.18-0.30 means — not strong evidence. High dose nearest was actually Protein degradation (similarity 0.339) consistent with lactacystin, but tally dilution pushed vote to DNA replication. Microscopist e7 correctly flagged enlarged, spread cells with pale DAPI, retained filamentous tubulin, no mitotic arrest — ruling out microtubule/Eg5/Aurora but calling unknown; I underweighted this and over-interpreted shared DNA-intensity changes that occur in both replication stress and proteasome-inhibition induced G1/G2 arrest/hypertrophy due to blocked protein turnover.

Proteasome inhibition can mimic DNA replication phenotype via cell-cycle arrest and altered chromatin accessibility without true tubulin or mitotic signatures, explaining low DAPI at high dose.

Future: proteasome activity assay + ubiquitin/p21 accumulation, EdU/PI flow, gamma-H2AX vs reference proteasome inhibitors to discriminate.

reflection.text:
Unblinding: lactacystin is a 20S proteasome inhibitor PMID 39988264, PMID 27802243 - truth MoA Protein degradation. My submitted conclusion DNA replication (p=0.41) was scored incorrect.

What the evidence got right:
- The phenotype was not cytoskeletal/anti-mitotic. I correctly down-weighted Aurora kinase inhibitors / Eg5 / microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers and actin disruptors because despite e6 k-neighbour 5/10 Aurora calls, the acquired wells showed no increased mitotic fraction (e14 rho=-0.95), no large/polyploid nucleus enrichment (e17 rho=+0.20, e16 rho=0.00), no disrupted tubulin (e15 rho=+0.80 weak, e7/e8 microscopist 'candidates: unknown/none'), and only modest cell loss.
- I captured dose-dependent hypertrophy: cell_area rho=+1.00 e11, cell_nuc_area_ratio rho=+1.00 e13, with high-dose values cell_nuc_area_ratio z=+9.3 and cell_area z=+4.3 at 3 uM e5 and z=+9.3 at 10 uM e2. That hypertrophy plus cell loss is compatible in retrospect with proteasome inhibition, and I had listed Protein degradation at 0.14 in hypothesis_history step 18 with e2,e11 as supporting.
- I recognized the atlas was weak: NSC 2/4 DNA replication and split k-NN, with similarities 0.17-0.34 as reviewer noted, and with only 4 wells x 1 replicate each. Stating p=0.41 was appropriately not overconfident, but still pointed to the wrong class.

What misled me and what I missed:
- Biphasic nuclear DNA intensity misinterpreted. e3 at 0.3 uM showed nuc_dna_mean z=+5.4, integrated z=+4.4, while e5 at 3 uM showed z=-5.2 and e2 at 10 uM z=-8.4. Across the 4 acquired wells dose_response gave perfect monotonic rho=-1.00 for nuc_dna_mean e9 and integrated e10. I used that monotonic fall + cell enlargement + count loss e12 rho=-0.80 to favor DNA replication (S-phase depletion) over DNA damage, arguing damage should increase DNA content per review. In doing so I treated e3 high DNA at 0.3 uM as the low-dose tail of a replication-inhibition curve, and low DNA at high doses as replication depletion, rather than as a proteasome-inhibitor response.
- I explicitly listed e3 and e9 as contradicting Protein degradation in hypothesis_history, because I expected proteasome inhibition not to produce opposite DNA mean shifts at 0.3 vs 3-10 uM. That expectation was wrong for this compound/context, and I had no reference signature for Protein degradation in e6 (0/10 k-neighbours, 0/4 NSC) to correct it. Lookup after submit e20/e21 returned 'none curated' in ChEMBL, so prior was low, and search_literature e22 for lactacystin proteasome inhibitor was only run post-submit - not available to revise hypotheses.
- Acquisition choice amplified the error. I sampled only 0.3,1,3,10 uM (e2-e5). That bracketed the reversal but dose_response over those 4 points collapsed the biphasic pattern into a single negative rho, hiding the non-monotonicity that would have been clearer with the 4 unacquired low doses 0.003-0.1 uM from e1. With no low-dose baseline, I could not test whether 0.3 uM +5.4 was a transient G2 accumulation / arrest effect of proteasome inhibition versus true DNA accumulation.
- No orthogonal proteasome read-out was acquired. I proposed EdU/PI/gamma-H2AX/p21/proteasome activity in next_experiment, but submitted before running it. Search e23 'proteasome inhibition cell enlargement reduced DNA staining cell cycle arrest' returned 0 hits in this run, so I had no literature anchor in-run to link hypertrophy + reduced DNA staining to proteasome inhibition, whereas I did have atlas signal for DNA replication. Proteasome roles are documented in the returned literature PMID 30865843, PMID 16905641, PMID 15966900 but I did not integrate phenotype-to-MoA mapping for this class pre-submit.

Lesson: For strongly hypertrophic hits with cell_nuc_area_ratio z>>3 and falling DNA mean/intensity at high dose but high DNA at mid dose, retain Protein degradation/proteasome inhibition as competing hypothesis even when NSC/k-NN favors replication/Aurora and ChEMBL has no curated mechanism. Future runs need: a) inclusion of proteasome inhibitor references in atlas, b) sampling full 8-point dose range with replicates at low doses to resolve biphasic DNA, c) immediate ubiquitin-conjugate accumulation / proteasome activity assay rather than relying on DNA intensity trends alone.

Search e23 'proteasome inhibition cell enlargement reduced DNA staining cell cycle arrest' returned 0 hits in this run, so I had no literature anchor in-run to link hypertrophy + reduced DNA staining to proteasome inhibition, whereas I did have atlas signal for DNA replication. Proteasome roles are documented in the returned literature PMID 30865843, PMID 16905641, PMID 15966900 but I did not integrate phenotype-to-MoA mapping for this class pre-submit.

Lesson: For strongly hypertrophic hits with cell_nuc_area_ratio z>>3 and falling DNA mean/intensity at high dose but high DNA at mid dose, retain Protein degradation/proteasome inhibition as competing hypothesis even when NSC/k-NN favors replication/Aurora and ChEMBL has no curated mechanism. Future runs need: a) inclusion of proteasome inhibitor references in atlas, b) sampling full 8-point dose range with replicates at low doses to resolve biphasic DNA, c) immediate ubiquitin-conjugate accumulation / proteasome activity assay rather than relying on DNA intensity trends alone.

What was right:
- Excluded microtubule/Aurora/actin despite e6 5/10 Aurora neighbours because e14-e17 and e7/e8 showed no mitosis/polyploidy/tubulin disruption
- Captured dose-dependent hypertrophy e11 rho=+1.00 and e13 rho=+1.00 with high-dose z=+9.3 e2 consistent with proteasome inhibitor hypertrophy
- Recognized weak atlas support NSC 2/4 split k-NN and single-replicate limitation, stated modest 0.41 probability

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted monotonic rho=-1.00 for nuc_dna_mean/integrated e9/e10 plus enlarged cells as DNA replication depletion, discounting biphasic e3 z=+5.4 at 0.3 uM vs e2 z=-8.4 at 10 uM as contradicting protein degradation
- Over-weighted e6 DNA replication vote despite low similarity and absent protein degradation neighbours; under-weighted hypertrophy signal for protein degradation (0.14 vs truth)
- Ran lookup/search only after submit e20-e23 so lactacystin as proteasome inhibitor PMID 39988264 PMID 27802243 not used to correct hypothesis ranking

Proposed next experiment: Do not use clinical advice - research screening only: repeat full 8-dose curve in duplicate plus 24h proteasome activity (Suc-LLVY-AMC) and K48-ubiquitin IF, co-stained EdU/PI cell-cycle profile and cell/nuclear area, versus reference proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib, MG132) and DNA replication inhibitors (aphidicolin, hydroxyurea) to test whether biphasic DNA intensity + hypertrophy maps to proteasome inhibition rather than replication.
